experiments.title: LED Blink
experiments.objective: Master basic digital output by blinking an LED at different intervals. Understand GPIO pins, digitalWrite, and timing using delay().
procedureSteps: Connect LED positive leg to GPIO 5 through 220Ω resistor
Connect LED negative leg to GND
Upload the code to ESP32
Observe LED blinking pattern
experiments.expectedOutput: LED blinks on and off at 1-second intervals

experiments.title: Button Input
experiments.objective: Read digital input from a button and control an LED based on button state. Learn about digitalRead and debouncing.
procedureSteps: Connect button to GPIO 4 with 10kΩ pull-up resistor
Connect LED to GPIO 5 through 220Ω resistor
Upload code and press the button
LED should turn on when button is pressed
experiments.expectedOutput: LED lights up when button is pressed, turns off when released

experiments.title: PWM LED Dimming
experiments.objective: Control LED brightness using PWM (Pulse Width Modulation). Learn about analog output and brightness control.
procedureSteps: Connect LED to GPIO 5 through 220Ω resistor
Upload the PWM control code
Observe LED brightness changing smoothly
Try adjusting delay values to change fade speed
experiments.expectedOutput: LED fades in and out smoothly in a continuous loop

experiments.title: Automatic Light Detection
experiments.objective: Interface an LDR with the ESP32 to automatically detect ambient light levels and trigger an LED based on a threshold.
procedureSteps: Connect LDR with 10kΩ resistor as voltage divider to GPIO 34
Connect LED to GPIO 5
Upload code and observe Serial Monitor
Cover LDR to trigger LED
experiments.expectedOutput: LED turns on when light level drops below threshold value

experiments.title: Temperature Monitoring
experiments.objective: Read temperature and humidity data using a DHT22 sensor. Display real-time values over Serial Monitor and trigger alerts on threshold breach.
procedureSteps: Connect DHT22 data pin to GPIO 17
Add pull-up resistor (10kΩ) between data and VCC
Install DHT library through Arduino IDE
Upload code and open Serial Monitor
Observe temperature and humidity readings
experiments.expectedOutput: Serial Monitor displays temperature and humidity values updating every 2 seconds

experiments.title: Buzzer Control
experiments.objective: Drive a passive buzzer with the ESP32 using PWM signals. Generate different tones by varying frequency and create simple alarm patterns.
procedureSteps: Connect buzzer positive to GPIO 12, negative to GND
Upload code to ESP32
Buzzer should play alternating tones
Try changing frequency values for different pitches
experiments.expectedOutput: Buzzer produces alternating tones (1000Hz and 1500Hz) with 500ms duration each

experiments.title: WiFi Connection
experiments.objective: Connect ESP32 to WiFi network and display connection status. Learn about WiFi libraries and network debugging.
procedureSteps: Replace YOUR_SSID and YOUR_PASSWORD with actual WiFi credentials
Upload code to ESP32
Open Serial Monitor at 115200 baud
Watch connection progress and obtain IP address
experiments.expectedOutput: Serial Monitor shows connection dots, then displays local IP address and signal strength updates

experiments.title: Motion Detection
experiments.objective: Interface a PIR (Passive Infrared) motion sensor with ESP32. Detect motion and trigger alerts or notifications.
procedureSteps: Connect PIR sensor output to GPIO 13
Connect LED to GPIO 5
Upload code and wait 30-60 seconds for sensor warm-up
Move in front of sensor to trigger detection
experiments.expectedOutput: LED lights up and serial prints 'Motion detected!' when movement is detected

experiments.title: Servo Motor Control
experiments.objective: Control servo motor angle using PWM signals. Learn servo protocols and precision angle positioning.
procedureSteps: Connect servo signal to GPIO 15, VCC to 5V, GND to GND
Install ESP32Servo library
Upload code to ESP32
Observe servo sweeping 0-180 degrees
experiments.expectedOutput: Servo motor sweeps from 0° to 180° smoothly and back in continuous cycle

experiments.title: Smart Home Scene
experiments.objective: Combine multiple sensors and actuators to create an integrated smart home scene with WiFi control.
procedureSteps: Connect all components as per pin assignments
Upload integrated control code
Test button control - should activate LED and buzzer
Test light sensor - should activate LED when dark
Experiment with combining different sensor inputs
experiments.expectedOutput: System responds to button and light level independently and in combination
